quote: Automatic generation of question-answer pairs (QA pairs) is a widely studied problem... this work examines QA pair generation corresponding to a news article summary paired with a self-contained question.
We propose a model for generating QA pairs with self-contained and summary-centric questions and length-constrained article-summarizing answers.
In this paper, we study QA pair generation corresponding to variable length article-summarizing answers paired with self-contained and summarycentric questions.
outputs: self-contained questions paired with length-constrained summary answers (QA pairs)

We conduct human evaluation on Amazon Mechanical Turk. We designed 7 annotation tasks (ATs).
guideline: Annotators were asked: 'Without referring to the answer or the article, are you able to understand the question?', 'Does the passage in the Answer text box answer the question?', 'Does the question capture the gist of the Article?'
Human annotators assess QA pairs on multiple annotation tasks (AT-1 to AT-5) covering self-containment, answer correctness, succinctness/sufficiency, and gist capture, with majority vote aggregation.

AT-1: Without referring to the answer or the article, are you able to understand the question? (Is the question self-contained?) AT-2: Does the passage in the Answer text box answers the question? AT-5: Does the question in the Question text box capture the gist of the Article? AT-6: Which Question shown above best captures the gist of the Article?
criteria: captures the gist of the article
